Q: SQL - ORDER BY - Threads & Messages A:

Your data structure does not make clear the relationship be messages and message user. My assumption is that these are joined on both thread_id and user_id. This then aggregates them at the thread level:

select t.thread_id
from thread t join
     message m
     on t.thread_id = m.thread_id join
     message_users mu
     on m.thread_id = mu.thread_id and
        m.user_id = mu.user_id
group by thread_id
order by max(mu.notify) desc, max(m.date_created) desc

The key to this is the final order by. Order by notify first, but descending so 1 appears before 0 (assuming non-1 value is 0). Then by date_created.

To restrict this to a particular user, use a WHERE statement before the group by:

WHERE u.user_id = session_user_id

Q: Local HTML file embed youtube with <iframe> A:

Just don't navigate to the file URI. You can usually bypass the file/// local resource origin issue (or opaque origin issue) when navigating to the raw file content instead of navigating to the file as a local resource or by making the local resource to a virtual host.

Local files are not classified as a safe origin by most browsers. They classify it as unsafe and as an opaque origin.

From the browser AI on opaque origin:

An opaque origin is a browser-internal security value used to obscure or nullify the true origin of a resource, ensuring it is never considered equal to any other origin, including other opaque origins. These are serialized as null and are applied when a resource’s origin is sensitive, non-existent, or unsafe for standard security checks, such as in sandboxed iframes, file:// URLs, or documents created via APIs like DOMImplementation.createDocument().

So YouTube only sees NULL as the site origin and treats that as suspicious.

Normal hosted page:

Parent URL: http://127.0.0.1:5500/testvideo.html
Origin: http://127.0.0.1:5500

YouTube sees a normal web origin.

Local file page:

Parent URL: file:///C:/.../testvideo.html
Origin: null / opaque / not a normal web origin

YouTube sees no acceptable hosting origin.

Solution 1

Use File.ReadAllTextAsync to read the HTML file into a string and then use WebView2 to navigate to the raw file content.

Basically

string htmlFilePath = "path/to/testvideo.html";
string htmlContent = await File.ReadAllTextAsync(htmlFilePath);

// Call this line once in your application 
// to properly initialise the control
await webView.EnsureCoreWebView2Async()

// Navigate to raw HTML
_webView2.NavigateToString(htmlContent);

This should work for your small HTML. But you should know that WebView2.NavigateToString has a limit of 2 MB file size. For simple HTML this is enough. But for huge files that may also inline scripts you may hit that limit. The documentation of the WebView2.NavigateToString method notes:

The htmlContent parameter may not be larger than 2 MB (2 * 1024 * 1024 bytes) in total size. The origin of the new page is about:blank.

Solution 2

An alternative solution that avoids the 2 MB limit is to map the file resource to a virtual host name:

// Call this line once in your application 
// to properly initialise the control
await webView.EnsureCoreWebView2Async();

// Example based on Microsoft Docs
string htmlRootDirectory = "path/to/html/location";
webView.CoreWebView2.SetVirtualHostNameToFolderMapping(
    "appassets.example", "htmlRootDirectory", CoreWebView2HostResourceAccessKind.DenyCors);
webView.Source = new Uri("https://appassets.example/testvideo.html");

As you can see, the mapping allows you to navigate to the local file as if it was a served remote resource. The mapped file is now virtually hosted by the specified virtual host (here appassets.example).

appassets.example maps to the directory which contains the HTML files. You can now use the host URL to navigate to any HTML file in that mapped directory.

See Microsoft Docs for additional remarks on virtual host name mapping.

Q: Error while loading excel file with Openpyxl A:

It is an issue with the file. When we saved the file externally it was prompting this error. easy fix is to make a try catch and if the it gives the error create a new file in the same name and save on the same place. But for appending with old data wont work in this case.

try:
    # this statement shall raise error for Badzip file
    wb_obj = openpyxl.load_workbook(filename=path)
except:
    # try to create a new file and save at same path
    wb_obj = openpyxl.Workbook()
    wb_obj.save(path)
    wb_obj = openpyxl.load_workbook(filename=path)

Q: Vite Dev Server Sourcemaps Don't Work or Point to Wrong Lines/Files in VScode Debugger A:

After much agony and investigation, I find that the root cause for the trouble with VSCode + Angular & Vite is:

Vite 'optimizes' (transforms) the javascript as it pushes it to the browser. And there is (currently 2/2025) no way for VSCode to get the actual code the browser is running. So the Chrome debugger works just fine (having the actual code), but VSCode is running the sourcemaps against the original source in node_modules/... and will generally be off by many lines (as Vite may insert newlines as it transforms the code)

Apparently this hack is no longer necessary (angular post v17?);
vite now has a config flag to disable the optimization tranforms. and Angular knows how to set it in { builder.configurations.development: { optimization: false }
So now development builds will correctly set breakpoints!

The only solution to keep VScode debugger sync'd with source is to revert to Webpack.

That's was pretty simple: angular.json projects.${myproject}.architect.build.builder:

Edit: Also change: "browser": "src/main.ts" --> "main": "src/main.ts"
